mem.t: As each has received a gift, employ it in serving one another, as good managers of the grace of God in its various forms.

lessons.title: Gifts Are for Building Up the Body
lessons.theme: Gifts are not medals awarded to individuals but presents given to the body

v: Now there are various kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit.
There are various kinds of service, and the same Lord.
There are various kinds of workings, but the same God who works all things in all.
But to each one is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the profit of all.

lessons.still: Rest your open hands on your knees and breathe quietly. Say to the Lord, “Lord, everything in my hands is something you have given.” Think back over what you have received from the Lord this year; don't rush to use any of it — first, simply give thanks.
teach: When a big family gathers for a holiday, someone cooks, someone washes up, someone chats with the grandparents, someone makes the children laugh. If everyone fought to do the cooking, the kitchen would be packed while no one was at the table looking after the guests. Gifts are like the division of tasks in a household: not for comparing who matters most, but for bringing the whole family to life.

Three times in a row Paul says “various kinds” — gifts, service and workings all differ; and three times he says “the same” — the same Spirit, the same Lord, the same God. The source of all this variety is the one triune God. Verse 7 is the key: “to each one is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the profit of all.” Gifts are not aimed inward to fulfil ourselves but outward to benefit others.

So gifts are not badges of spiritual status, nor capital for building a personal brand. Before asking, “What gifts do I have?” first ask, “For whom were they given?” Once our mindset turns — from “mine” to “the Lord's,” from “for myself” to “for the body” — gifts stop being a source of pride and become channels of service.
lessons.light: 321 Light: When gifts are seized by the self-ruled life, they become power to exalt ourselves; only when handed back to the Lord do they become building materials for God's kingdom system. When Jesus reigns, our gifts have their rightful owner; when Jesus receives the glory, our gifts have their rightful direction.
q: Who is God? — The triune God is one, yet works in such varied ways. What does that teach you about him?
Who am I? — Have you ever treated a gift as your own achievement or as a label of identity?
How shall I respond? — What has the Lord given you that you can use today for someone else's benefit?
lessons.jesus: Jesus was full of the Holy Spirit and had great power to heal, cast out demons and teach, yet he never used it to turn stones into bread for himself or to win applause. Every display of his power was for the good of others and the glory of the Father.
lessons.pray: Holy Spirit, thank you for giving gifts to me — not because I deserve them, but because you love your church. Remove from me any desire to use my gifts to exalt myself, and let everything in my hands become a blessing to others. May all glory be to the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: List three things others have told you were “really helpful”
Write a note of thanks to someone in your church who serves quietly
Today, use something you are good at to help someone, without being asked
lessons.noon: “But to each one is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the profit of all.” — Lord, right now make me a blessing to others.

lessons.title: The Picture of the Body
lessons.theme: In the body of Christ, no one is unnecessary

v: The eye can’t tell the hand, “I have no need for you,” or again the head to the feet, “I have no need for you.”
No, much rather, those members of the body which seem to be weaker are necessary.
When one member suffers, all the members suffer with it. When one member is honored, all the members rejoice with it.
Now you are the body of Christ, and members individually.

lessons.still: Slowly become aware of your body from head to toe: your eyes, your hands, your feet, and your heart, unseen yet beating all the time. Say to the Lord, “Thank you for making me, and for placing me in your body.”
teach: Your little finger seems insignificant, but catch it in a door and your whole body stops — even your voice changes. A body is never a set of independent parts; it is one life in which every part feels the others: when one place hurts, the whole body knows.

Paul is dealing with two errors here. One is “the eye can't tell the hand, ‘I have no need for you’” — thinking ourselves strong and looking down on others. The other, a little earlier, is the foot saying, “Because I'm not the hand, I'm not part of the body” — thinking ourselves weak and giving up on ourselves. The first is pride, the second self-pity, but both are focused on self. Verses 26–27 give the answer: we suffer together and rejoice together, because “you are the body of Christ.”

The church is not a collection of individual believers but a living organism. When I learn to rejoice in others' success and weep over others' pain, I am no longer a spectator sitting in a meeting but a member living in the body. This is also the soil for 235 relationships: without an awareness of the body, there can be no real companions or teams.
lessons.light: 321 Light: People matter more than tasks; relationships matter more than things. In the body, the focus is not on who is more visible but on Christ the Head. Humility lets me admit, “I need you”; the self-emptied life makes me willing to say, “Your joy is my joy” — this is a body united.
q: Who is God? — God deliberately regards the “weaker” members as indispensable. What does that show you about him?
Who am I? — Are you more likely to say “I have no need for you” or “I am not part of the body”?
How shall I respond? — Who in your church is suffering or being honoured right now, and needs you to share in it?
lessons.jesus: The risen Jesus appeared to Saul, who was persecuting the church, and said, “Why are you persecuting me?” To persecute the members is to persecute the Head. He is the Head; he feels the pain in every part of the body and intercedes before the Father for every member.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, thank you that you are the Head and I am a member of your body. Forgive me for looking down on others, and forgive me for looking down on myself. Teach me to weep with those who weep and rejoice with those who rejoice; let me live within your body and no longer fight alone. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Say to a brother or sister you have looked down on, “I need you”
Pray specifically for a member of your church who is suffering
Sincerely congratulate a co-worker on something they have achieved
lessons.noon: “Now you are the body of Christ, and members individually.” — Lord, right now let my heart beat together with your body.

lessons.title: Discovering My Gifts
lessons.theme: Thinking of ourselves soberly, and recognising our gifts as we serve

v: For I say through the grace that was given me, to everyone who is among you, not to think of yourself more highly than you ought to think; but to think reasonably, as God has apportioned to each person a measure of faith.
having gifts differing according to the grace that was given to us: if prophecy, let’s prophesy according to the proportion of our faith;
or service, let’s give ourselves to service; or he who teaches, to his teaching;
or he who exhorts, to his exhorting; he who gives, let him do it with generosity; he who rules, with diligence; he who shows mercy, with cheerfulness.

lessons.still: Become still and ask the Holy Spirit to help you remember: when have you served others and felt especially joyful inside, while they were especially helped? Don't evaluate; just let the scenes come to mind one by one, and write them down.
teach: You don't know how deep a well is just by digging it; you find out by lowering the bucket and drawing water. Many people want to “measure” their gifts first before they start serving, but gifts are often discovered in the course of serving. It is like learning to swim: however many manuals you read on the shore, you only find out whether you can float once you get in the water.

Paul first says, “not to think of yourself more highly than you ought to think; but to think reasonably,” and only then talks about gifts. Overestimating ourselves is pride; underestimating ourselves is another form of self-centredness. The gifts he lists are very down-to-earth: prophecy, service, teaching, exhorting, giving, leading, showing mercy — and each comes with an attitude: wholehearted, generous, diligent, cheerful. Gifts joined to character are what become a blessing.

There are three clues to discovering your gifts: the burden in your heart (what do I often care deeply about?), confirmation from others (how do people find me helpful?), and the fruit of the Spirit (does life flow out when I do it?). The best way is to try serving within your “2” and “3” relationships, letting your spiritual companions and spiritual parents help you see what you cannot see in yourself.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Thinking reasonably about ourselves means returning to our place — letting people be people and letting God be God. The Holy Spirit is my guide; he distributes gifts to each one. Jesus is my example; he displayed his gifts in serving. A change of mindset: no longer knowing myself through comparison, but through what God has apportioned.
q: Who is God? — God apportions “to each person a measure of faith.” What does that show you about his wisdom?
Who am I? — Are you more prone to overestimate yourself or to underestimate yourself?
How shall I respond? — Which spiritual companion or spiritual parent will you ask to tell you what gifts they see in you?
lessons.jesus: At twelve Jesus was listening, asking and answering in the temple, yet he began his public ministry only after his baptism at thirty. He knew clearly what the Father had sent him to do, so he was not driven by the crowd's expectations. The root of knowing our gifts is knowing our relationship with the Father.
lessons.pray: Lord, help me think of myself with sober judgement — neither proud nor self-deprecating. Holy Spirit, open my eyes to recognise the gifts you have placed in me, and give me a heart that is wholehearted, generous, diligent and cheerful in using them. May I be used by you, not bound by comparison. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down three experiences of serving in which you felt joy and others were helped
Ask a spiritual companion to tell you what gifts they see in you
Try a small form of service this week that you have never done before
lessons.noon: “But to think reasonably” — Lord, right now let me see myself through your eyes.

lessons.title: Love Is the Most Excellent Way
lessons.theme: Without love, even the greatest gift counts for nothing

v: But earnestly desire the best gifts. Moreover, I show a most excellent way to you.
If I speak with the languages of men and of angels, but don’t have love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal.
If I have the gift of prophecy, and know all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have all faith, so as to remove mountains, but don’t have love, I am nothing.
If I give away all my goods to feed the poor, and if I give my body to be burned, but don’t have love, it profits me nothing.

lessons.still: Call to mind, one by one, the acts of service you will do today, and quietly place one word in front of each: “love.” Gently ask the Lord, “Am I doing this out of love, or for myself?” Then listen.
teach: Even the finest sound system, unplugged, is just a silent box; and if the current is faulty, it produces only harsh noise. Gifts are like the sound system, and love is like the current. Gifts without love are not merely useless — they can even hurt people.

The Corinthian church had many gifts yet was full of quarrels. Between chapters 12 and 14, where he discusses gifts, Paul deliberately placed a chapter on love. In one breath he lists the most admired gifts — tongues, prophecy, knowledge, mountain-moving faith, even self-sacrifice — and concludes: without love, I am a clanging cymbal, I am nothing, it profits me nothing. The most excellent way is not one more gift; it is the road every gift must travel.

Here we need a change of perspective: from “What can I do?” to “How do I love people?” The test of service is not how big the event is or how much applause there is, but whether the person being served has felt God's love. People matter more than tasks; if we hurt people for the sake of getting things done well, we have already strayed from the most excellent way.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Love is the self-emptied life — living for Jesus and for others, not for ourselves. Gifts belong to “ministry”; love belongs to “life”: life first, then relationships, then ministry. In 920, love heads the ninefold fruit of the Spirit, precisely so that our gifts operate in the soil of that fruit.
q: Who is God? — Why does God regard love as greater than every gift?
Who am I? — Have there been times in your service when you became “sounding brass or a clanging cymbal”?
How shall I respond? — In which act of service today will you choose first to love the person?
lessons.jesus: The Gospels often record that before a miracle Jesus was “moved with compassion.” When he healed a man with leprosy, he first reached out and touched him — his power healed the body, and his touch healed a heart long cut off from others. Everything he did flowed out of love.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, I confess that in my service I have sometimes cared more about results than about people. Fill me with your love, so that what I do is no longer sounding brass or a clanging cymbal. Let me love people first and then serve them; let what people sense in me be you. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Before an act of service begins, spend one minute praying for the person you will serve
Apologise to someone you have treated impatiently while serving
Today, offer a warm look or greeting in place of a correction
lessons.noon: “I show a most excellent way to you.” — Lord, right now let me walk in the way of love.

lessons.title: Serving One Another with Our Gifts
lessons.theme: Being good stewards of God's varied grace, so that God is glorified in all things

v: As each has received a gift, employ it in serving one another, as good managers of the grace of God in its various forms.

If anyone speaks, let it be as it were the very words of God. If anyone serves, let it be as of the strength which God supplies, that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom belong the glory and the dominion forever and ever. Amen.

lessons.still: Take a deep breath and imagine the Lord placing a bunch of keys in your hand, each one a gift. They are not given for you to collect, but for you to open other people's doors. Say to the Lord, “Lord, I am your steward.”
teach: A steward lives in his master's great house and holds all the keys; he can deploy every resource, yet he knows full well that none of it is his. A good steward's joy lies not in owning but in seeing the master's household run well and the master pleased.

Peter says “each” — there is no believer without a gift; “serving one another” — gifts flow within relationships; “in its various forms” — God's grace comes in a thousand shapes. Verse 11 divides gifts into two broad kinds, speaking and serving, and the principle is the same for both: speak as the very words of God, serve by the strength God supplies. And the purpose is one: “that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ.”

This week we have seen that gifts are for building up the body (Day 1), that I belong within the body (Day 2), how to recognise our gifts (Day 3), and that love is the way (Day 4); today we put it into practice as stewards who serve. Next week we will see how God forms people with different gifts into teams — fellow soldiers in the fivefold ministry, equipping the saints together.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The path of service — Spirit, Word, Life, Reign, God: serving by the Holy Spirit's guidance, according to the truth of Scripture, living out the life of Jesus, letting Jesus reign, and finally giving the glory to God. The goal of our gifts is not that I am seen, but that “to him belong the glory and the dominion.”
q: Who is God? — God has entrusted his varied gifts to people like you. What does that teach you about him?
Who am I? — Are you like a collector who locks gifts away, or a steward who keeps them circulating?
How shall I respond? — Which gift will you use this week to serve a spiritual companion or one of your spiritual children?
lessons.jesus: Jesus prayed to the Father, “I glorified you on the earth. I have accomplished the work which you have given me to do.” He was the Father's most faithful steward, giving glory to the Father through a lifetime of service and finally laying down even his life.
lessons.pray: Father God, thank you for entrusting your varied gifts to me. I am not the owner but the steward. Help me speak according to your word and serve in your strength, not for my own reputation, but so that in all things you may be glorified through Jesus Christ. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Choose one gift to use this week and write down whom you will serve with it
After completing an act of service, pray silently, “Glory to you”
Invite one of your spiritual children to serve alongside you once
lessons.noon: “As each has received a gift, employ it in serving one another.” — Lord, right now I am your faithful steward.
